acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Ira talks with Zoe Chace about watching Trump’s victory from an ecstatic room in Michigan. Then he checks in with a DC cop who was injured at the Capitol on January 6.
acts.credits: By Ira Glass and Zoe Chace

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Trump has claimed that he will be able to deport between 15 and 20 million people. But neither he nor his team have spelled out exactly how they’d do it. Producer Nadia Reiman looked into what mass deportation could actually look like on the ground if and when it comes to pass.
acts.title: The Largest Deportation Operation in American History

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Trump won record numbers of Latino voters this year. Ike Sriskandarajah spent the day with a guy in Pennsylvania who's been working to bring Latino voters to Trump for years.
acts.title: Nobody Loves Our Latino Community and our Puerto Rican Community More Than I Do

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Ira talks with two of Trump’s “political enemies” about their post-election plans.
acts.title: Sometimes Revenge Can Be Justified

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc:
Ten different states had abortion rights measures on their ballots this election. Producer Miki Meek got curious about a particular kind of political ad that aired in many of those states and called up a few of the women whose stories were featured in them.
We first learned about Deborah Dorbert and Kimberly Paseka from articles in The Washington Post.
acts.credits: By Miki Meek; Edited by Dana Chivvis; Additional reporting by Henry Larson
acts.title: I’ve Done an Unbelievable Job on the Abortion Question
